symptom: On Windows, `mxcli marketplace diff` / `update` fail building the reference project: `Extracting module files into C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Temp\mxdiff1185592798\target-ref` then `The specified file name or path is too long, or a component of the specified path is too long.` Works with `TMP=C:\mxt`.
cause: mx refuses any file path of 260+ characters ITSELF (Mendix FileSystem.OpenNewFileForWriting throws PathTooLongException), on every OS. The reference project was built in os.MkdirTemp("", "mxdiff")/target-ref — %TEMP% is ~28+len(user) on Windows — and bundled node_modules reach 181 (11.12.1 blank template) to ~202 (NanoflowCommons 7.x) characters, so 7.x fit for no user name.
file: `cmd/mxcli/marketplace/workdir.go` (`NewWorkDir`, `workRoot`, `mxFailure`, `mxMaxPath`), callers in `cmd/mxcli/cmd_marketplace_{diff,update,install}.go` (one-letter slot dirs), `scratch.go` (hint on mx failure); tests `workdir_test.go`, `workdir_integration_test.go` (-tags integration, real mx)
insight: The 'Windows-only' bug reproduces on Linux: the first `mx create-project` in the scratchpad (~85-char path) threw PathTooLongException, which is what exposed that the limit is mx's, not the OS's — then a bisection on base-dir length (77 ok / 78 fails for create-project; 259 ok / 260 fails for module-import of a 200-char entry) pinned it exactly, with the reported message verbatim. So no Windows box is needed: point TMPDIR at a 48-char dir and import a package with one deep declared entry. Sizing came from the deepest file in a real blank app plus the npm tarballs NanoflowCommons 7.x pins (registry.npmjs.org is reachable; marketplace downloads need a PAT). Wrong turns to skip: a relative .mpr or --output-dir does not help (mx resolves to absolute, and create-project --output-dir ./x throws UriFormatException); and a drive-root default like C:\mxt is NOT safe — children of C:\ inherit Authenticated Users:Modify, so another account could swap the package before import. Shortest PRIVATE root wins (%USERPROFILE%\.mxcli\t, /tmp via 0700 MkdirTemp, or TMP/TMPDIR if shorter); that still bounds the Windows user name at ~22 chars for 202-char packages, hence the hint naming dir, length and remaining budget.
